key_insight: LLIFT generates semi-synthetic brain MRI images with realistic, user-controlled lesion locations, enabling ground-truth benchmarks for evaluating XAI methods without needing pixel-level lesion labels.
clinical_relevance: This could improve how explainable AI tools are tested in medical imaging by providing more realistic lesion-containing images than hand-crafted perturbations or annotation-dependent workflows.
method: LLIFT learns pathological features from binary class labels rather than lesion annotations.
LLIFT-GAN uses a custom GAN to transfer local disease-like features into healthy brain MRI.
LLIFT-DM uses diffusion-based inpainting with ControlNet and bounding-box masks to place lesions in chosen regions.
evidence_signal: On Human Connectome Project brain MRI data, both GAN- and diffusion-based versions achieved Fréchet Inception Distance scores comparable to the healthy-vs-pathological gap in the dataset, with qualitative review indicating realistic lesion structures.
watch_item: The approach is benchmark-oriented and synthetic, so performance may depend on how well generated lesions capture the full diversity and clinical nuance of real pathology.
paper_title: Local Label-Informed Feature Transfer for Generating Ground-Truth Medical Images: A Comparison of GAN- and Diffusion-Based Approaches
